requirements.title: Image termination does not finalize entities that already exist
requirements.definition: On image execution termination by an error, STOP statement, ERROR STOP statement, or END PROGRAM statement, entities existing immediately before termination are not finalized.

pending.end-program-suppresses-existing-entity-f: PENDING plan: main program creates a nonsaved local finalizable object with token 17. Its FINAL subroutine writes `FINAL-17` to OUTPUT_UNIT and calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT). The program writes and flushes `BEFORE-END-17`, then reaches END PROGRAM. Assert stdout contains `BEFORE-END-17` and does not contain `FINAL-17`. A separate companion program calls a subroutine with the same nonsaved local type and returns normally; 7.5.6.3 S7.5.6.3-003 requires that companion to print and flush `FINAL-17`, proving the finalizer path is live.
pending.stop-stmt-suppresses-existing-entity-fin: PENDING plan: main program creates a nonsaved local finalizable object with token 23. Its FINAL subroutine writes `FINAL-23` to OUTPUT_UNIT and calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT). The program writes and flushes `BEFORE-STOP-23`, then executes STOP. Assert stdout contains `BEFORE-STOP-23` and does not contain `FINAL-23`; ignore any processor STOP banner and status wording. A separate normal-return companion using the same type prints and flushes `FINAL-23` under 7.5.6.3 S7.5.6.3-003.
pending.error-stop-stmt-suppresses-existing-enti: PENDING separate-program plan: module defines type t with a FINAL subroutine that writes `FINAL` to OUTPUT_UNIT and calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT). A subroutine declares a NONSAVED local `type(t) :: x`, writes `BEFORE`, calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT), then executes ERROR STOP. The oracle checks only stdout: it contains `BEFORE` and does not contain `FINAL`. Exit status, stop code, and processor banner text are not compared. The anti-vacuity companion is the same subroutine body with the ERROR STOP replaced by normal RETURN; under 7.5.6.3 S7.5.6.3-003 that companion does print and flush `FINAL`.
pending.error-termination-suppresses-existing-en: PENDING separate-program plan: module defines type t with a FINAL subroutine that writes `FINAL` to OUTPUT_UNIT and calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT). A subroutine declares a NONSAVED local `type(t) :: x` and an allocatable scalar `integer, allocatable :: a`, executes `allocate(a)`, writes `BEFORE`, calls FLUSH(OUTPUT_UNIT), then executes a second `allocate(a)` without STAT=. Because allocating an already allocated allocatable is an ALLOCATE error condition (9.7.1.3 S9.7.1.3-001) and 9.7.1.2 S9.7.1.2-013 says a no-STAT ALLOCATE error initiates error termination, the oracle checks only stdout: it contains `BEFORE` and does not contain `FINAL`. Exit status and processor diagnostic text are not compared. The anti-vacuity companion replaces the second ALLOCATE with normal RETURN and must print and flush `FINAL` under 7.5.6.3 S7.5.6.3-003.

requirements.oracle: Each plan observes only explicitly flushed stdout markers: the route-specific BEFORE marker must appear and the FINAL marker must not. Exit status, STOP/ERROR STOP codes, processor banners, allocation diagnostic text, finalization order among multiple entities, file closure timing, and multi-image behavior are not compared. Anti-vacuity comes from a companion ordinary subroutine-return program using the same type and FINAL subroutine; 7.5.6.3 S7.5.6.3-003 requires that companion to print the FINAL marker.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only packet records pending plans and creates no fixture approval. Error-termination plans compare only flushed stdout marker presence/absence, never process status, stop-code values, traceback text, banner wording, allocation status after termination, or resource-exhaustion behavior. The note is informative. Coarray, team, and multi-image termination behavior is outside this packet.
requirements.dependencies: Confirmed existing owner catalogues opened on main: doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_6_3.json S7.5.6.3-003 for ordinary nonsaved local finalization on normal RETURN/END; doc/catalogues/allocation_of_allocatable_variables_9_7_1_3.json S9.7.1.3-001 for allocating an already allocated allocatable as an ALLOCATE error condition; doc/catalogues/execution_of_allocate_statement_9_7_1_2.json S9.7.1.2-013 for no-STAT ALLOCATE error termination; doc/catalogues/save_attribute_8_5_16.json for SAVE. STOP/ERROR STOP and program termination catalogues are dependencies not re-owned here; 19.6 definition status remains a dependency.
